scope.one_liner: The developer platform for wearable health: we build the wearable, they build what's possible with it.

waves.focus: deepen investor lanes: partners behind each wearable round, warm paths
deepen growth and social: builders hurt by API sunsets, Ohio communities, creators
verify every link, de-duplicate, rank, publish the final board

lanes.title: Equity accelerators, corporate VCs and investor events
Athletes, teams and events Vybe could sponsor

targets.name: Alumni Ventures
targets.why: Co-invested in three wearable rounds in the last 12 months: SOND ($7M, in-ear HRV sleep), Emm ($9M seed, smart menstrual cup) and Wearlinq ($14M Series A, ECG wearable).
targets.warm_path: alumni network (AV runs alumni-affiliated funds; check founders' schools)
targets.ask: Add to co-investor list for the seed round
targets.opener: Hi AV team - you've been in SOND, Emm and Wearlinq this year. Vybe Health is a screenless ECG/HRV band with a licensed SDK/API, from a veteran/woman/minority-owned team in Akron. DevKit v0.1 goes to design partners this fall. Could we talk for 15 minutes about co-investing when our seed forms?

targets.name: Cade Ventures: 'Why we haven't invested in a wearable yet - and what would change our minds'
targets.why: On 23 Jun 2026 Ashley Pimlott and Isabel Glass of Cade, an earliest-stage investor in health tech, consumer tech and connected hardware, wrote that they get pitched wearables constantly. They are waiting for a company that measures something different for an underserved population and builds the 'decision layer'. They also note Google killed the Fitbit app and that 'YC is back funding wearable hardware'. This is a public, dated invitation to pitch against stated criteria.
targets.ask: Reply to Ashley Pimlott / Isabel Glass with a one-paragraph answer to each of their three criteria (adoption, commercialization timeline, differentiation).
targets.opener: Your wearable post was the most honest investor take we have read. Our answer to 'what would change our minds': Vybe is a screenless ECG/HRV band sold first as a developer platform (licensed SDK, DevKit to 5-10 design partners), then to consumers in May 2027 with no subscription. Open to a 15-minute conversation?

targets.name: Clair Health $11M seed led by Khosla for women's hormone wristband
targets.why: On 17 Jun 2026 Fortune reported that Clair Health (Jenny Duan, Abhinav Agarwal) closed an $11M seed for a 10-biosensor wristband that infers hormonal cycle phase from HRV, skin temperature and EDA. Khosla Ventures (partner Dr. Alex Morgan) led, with a16z speedrun, Brydge Club, Treehub, Cartan Capital, AGI House, Insiders VC and Anne Wojcicki. Morgan said much wearable tech is 'bro-tech for tech-bros', which matches Vybe's woman/minority-owned profile.
targets.ask: Ask Dr. Alex Morgan (Khosla) and the a16z speedrun team for a 15-minute conversation; Clair is also a possible SDK partner.
targets.opener: Your Clair lead and the 'bro-tech for tech-bros' line stood out. Vybe Health is a woman-, veteran- and minority-owned team in Akron building a screenless ECG/HRV band as a developer platform (licensed SDK, no subscription). Would you be open to a short conversation?

targets.name: Crosslink Capital
targets.why: Co-invested in SOND's $7M round for HRV/SCG-sensing sleep earbuds. Crosslink writes $1M-$9M initial checks at seed and Series A across North America.
targets.ask: 15-min intro call
targets.opener: Hi Crosslink team - I saw you backed SOND. I'm building Vybe Health in Akron, Ohio: a screenless ECG/HRV band plus licensed SDK/API so developers can build on clean cardiac data. DevKit v0.1 is in design-partner hands this fall. Would you be open to a short call to see if it fits your seed thesis?

targets.name: E14 Fund
targets.why: Led SOND's $7M round: Dreambuds, in-ear sleep platform sensing 12 signals incl. HRV and seismocardiography. E14 invests pre-seed to Series A in MIT-community founders.
targets.why_now: 2026-05-27: SOND exits stealth with $7M, round led by E14 Fund
targets.warm_path: MIT network required (E14 backs MIT-community founders)
targets.ask: 15-min intro call
targets.opener: Hi E14 team - congrats on leading SOND. I'm building Vybe Health, a screenless ECG/HRV band offered as a developer platform with a licensed SDK/API; DevKit v0.1 is going to 5-10 design partners now. Given your SOND thesis on body sensing as a platform, would someone on the team take a 15-minute call?

targets.name: FDA 2026 General Wellness guidance explicitly covers wearables measuring HRV, BP, SpO2
targets.why: On 6 Jan 2026 FDA issued a final revised General Wellness guidance replacing the 2019 version. It places non-invasive wearables that estimate HRV, blood pressure, oxygen saturation or glucose under enforcement discretion if outputs are for wellness only, do not prompt clinical action and do not mimic clinical values. This makes the regulatory path for Vybe's general-wellness ECG/HRV band clearer.
targets.ask: Map every Vybe feature and SDK output to the guidance guardrails; publish a short 'wellness-only' developer policy so design partners stay compliant.

targets.name: Fitbit Web API shuts down 30 Oct 2026; tokens do not migrate
targets.why: Google retired developer support for the legacy Fitbit Web API on 30 Sep 2026 and turns it off on 30 Oct 2026 (moved from 30 Sep). New Fitbit developer registrations are closed and OAuth grants do not carry over, so every app must re-consent users on the Google Health API. Vybe can pitch a licensed SDK/API with stable, owned access to raw ECG/HRV to builders hurt by this.
targets.why_now: 2026-10-30 shutdown (developer support ended 2026-09-30; Sahha update dated 2026-10-01)
targets.ask: Build a 'Fitbit API refugee' list (research apps, coaching apps, Fitabase-type study platforms) and offer DevKit v0.1 design-partner slots before 30 Oct.
targets.opener: If your product read Fitbit data through the Web API, the 30 Oct cutoff probably means a re-consent scramble. We are building a screenless ECG/HRV band with a licensed SDK and raw-data access, and we are picking 5-10 design partners for DevKit v0.1. Open to a 15-minute call on what your integration needs?

targets.name: Fortify Ventures
targets.why: US-based fund that co-led Samphire Neuroscience's $5M seed for Nettle, a neurotech headband wearable for menstrual symptoms. Fortify lists it under 'Human Health'.
targets.ask: 15-min intro call
targets.opener: Hi Fortify team - saw your co-lead on Samphire. Vybe Health is a woman/veteran/minority-owned team building a screenless ECG/HRV band with a licensed SDK/API for developers, no subscription. DevKit v0.1 goes to design partners this fall. Would you be open to a 15-minute conversation?

targets.name: Garmin launches CIRQA screenless band at $199.99, no subscription
targets.why: On 21 Jul 2026 Garmin announced CIRQA, its first screen-free smart band ($199.99, up to 10 days battery, HRV, Pulse Ox, skin temperature, no subscription), worn on the wrist or arm. It follows the $169.99 Index Sleep Monitor upper-arm band from 18 Jun 2025. Every major incumbent now ships a screenless band.
targets.ask: Add CIRQA and Index to the competitor matrix; highlight that neither offers ECG or an open raw-data SDK.

targets.name: Khosla Ventures
targets.why: Led Clair Health's $11.6M seed (continuous hormone wrist wearable, 10-sensor stack incl. HRV/skin temp) and led Somnee's $10M seed extension (EEG sleep headband). Two wearable seed leads in 12 months. Partner Alex Morgan (biotech/healthcare/data science) ran early digital-health trials with health wearables at Stanford per his KV bio.
targets.why_now: 2026-06-17: Clair Health $11.6M seed led by Khosla (also led Somnee seed extension 2025-06-10)
targets.ask: 15-min intro call
targets.opener: Hi Alex - I'm building Vybe Health in Akron: a screenless ECG/HRV band sold as a developer platform (SDK/API, DevKit v0.1 going to 5-10 design partners) rather than another subscription app. Clair and Somnee suggest KV sees sensors as a data layer others build on. Would you be open to a 15-minute conversation about how you think about wearable platforms at seed?

targets.name: Kiva Dickinson
targets.why: Selva led Kimba's $6.5M seed. Kimba is a bedside sleep device that senses breathing, movement and HRV and integrates with WHOOP/Oura/Apple Watch/Garmin. Selva leads seed and Series A in consumer health and wellness. Kimba's founder is a former special forces commander.
targets.why_now: 2026-06-16: Kimba $6.5M funding led by Selva Ventures
targets.ask: 15-min intro call
targets.opener: Hi Kiva - saw Selva led Kimba. We're Vybe Health, a veteran/woman/minority-owned team in Akron building a screenless ECG/HRV band: no subscription, general wellness, with an SDK so apps like Kimba can use clean cardiac data. Consumer launch is May 2027. Open to a 15-minute call?

targets.name: Kristina Simmons
targets.why: Overwater led Adaptyx's pre-seed and participated significantly in its $14M seed (continuous multi-analyte biowearable). Simmons published the 'always-on health tracking' investment memo. The site notes Overwater backed a team for its 'veteran experience', which points to an angle Vybe could use.
targets.why_now: 2025-10-20: Adaptyx $14M seed with significant Overwater participation + 'Why We Invested' post
targets.warm_path: veteran (Overwater site cites backing a team for its veteran experience)
targets.ask: 15-min intro call
targets.opener: Hi Kristina - your Adaptyx post on always-on health tracking stuck with me. I'm building Vybe Health, a veteran/woman/minority-owned team in Akron shipping a screenless ECG/HRV band as a developer platform (SDK/API, DevKit v0.1 to 5-10 design partners). Would you be open to a 15-minute conversation?

targets.name: Labcorp Venture Fund
targets.why: Labcorp Venture Fund joined Emm's $9M smart-cup seed. Labcorp also invested in Ultrahuman's $70M smart-ring round in Sept 2026. It is a strategic diagnostics investor active in both seed and growth wearable rounds.
targets.why_now: 2026-09-03: Labcorp in Ultrahuman $70M round; 2025-11-18 Emm seed
targets.ask: 15-min intro call
targets.opener: Hi - I'm the founder of Vybe Health, building a screenless ECG/HRV band with a licensed SDK/API, no subscription, general wellness. Labcorp's moves into Ultrahuman and Emm suggest you see wearables as a front door to diagnostics partnerships. Could we have a 15-minute conversation about how the venture fund approaches seed-stage hardware?

targets.name: Oscar Moralez
targets.why: Boomerang, a Midwest healthcare venture studio and fund focused on connected health tech, made a seed investment in SynchNeuro, a behind-the-ear EEG wearable tracking glucose, HRV, sleep and stress.
targets.why_now: 2025-11-12: Boomerang seed investment in SynchNeuro wearable
targets.warm_path: Midwest (Indianapolis-based; Vybe is in Akron, OH)
targets.ask: 15-min intro call
targets.opener: Hi Oscar - fellow Midwesterner here. Vybe Health in Akron is building a screenless ECG/HRV band and licensed SDK/API for connected-health developers; DevKit v0.1 goes to 5-10 design partners this fall. SynchNeuro shows Boomerang backs wearables at seed. Would you have 15 minutes for a conversation?

targets.name: Oura files S-1: $1.21B revenue in 9 months, ~5M paid members
targets.why: Oura's public S-1 was filed 3 Sep 2026 (Nasdaq: OURA). Revenue was $1.2B for the nine months to 30 Jun 2026, up from $697M a year earlier, with about 5M paid members and roughly 85% 12-month membership retention. These are public numbers on wearable subscription economics; Vybe's no-subscription model can be positioned against them.
targets.ask: Pull S-1 metrics into the investor deck's market slide; contrast the subscription model with Vybe's licensing plus no-subscription model.

targets.name: Oura postpones $2.1B IPO; early backers Forerunner and Lifeline named
targets.why: On 29 Sep 2026 Oura postponed an IPO that was set to raise about $2.1B at $40-44 a share, citing market conditions, despite being about 5x oversubscribed. Axios named the pre-IPO holders as Fidelity 10.9%, Forerunner Ventures 9.3%, Bedford Ridge 9.2% and Lifeline Ventures 7.3%. Forerunner and Lifeline backed Oura early and now hold large wearable stakes. Expect more debate on whether wearables are valued as health-tech or as consumer electronics.
targets.ask: Research Forerunner Ventures and Lifeline Ventures partners who led the early Oura rounds; ask for a 15-minute conversation about developer-platform wearables.
targets.opener: You backed Oura early, so you have seen the wearable category from seed to S-1. We are building Vybe Health in Akron: a screenless ECG/HRV band sold as a developer platform (licensed SDK/API, no subscription), with DevKit v0.1 going to 5-10 design partners. Would you be open to a short conversation?

targets.name: Resolute Ventures
targets.why: Participated in Kimba's $6.5M sleep-device seed (HRV and breathing sensing). Resolute leads pre-seed and seed rounds; portfolio includes Hello Heart (heart health) and Vercel (developer tools).
targets.ask: 15-min intro call
targets.opener: Hi Resolute team - with Hello Heart and Vercel in your portfolio, Vybe may sit right between them: a screenless ECG/HRV band whose core product is a developer SDK/API. DevKit v0.1 goes to 5-10 design partners this fall. Saw you in Kimba's seed too. Open to 15 minutes?

targets.name: SOND exits stealth with $7M (E14 Fund lead) for HRV-sensing sleep earbuds
targets.why: On 18 Jun 2026 SOND (Boston; founded by Bose's former Head of Global Sleep Products) announced $7M led by MIT-affiliated E14 Fund, with Crosslink Capital and Ubiquity Ventures, plus John Abele, Alumni Ventures and Meach Cove. Dreambuds capture 12 signals overnight, including HRV and seismocardiography. These are seed-stage hardware investors backing biometric sensing.
targets.ask: Ask E14 Fund and Ubiquity Ventures (hardware/sensing seed) for a conversation; reference the SOND deal.
targets.opener: Congrats on SOND. We are building the wrist counterpart for developers: a screenless ECG/HRV band with a licensed SDK, general wellness only, with DevKit v0.1 going to design partners this year. Would a 15-minute conversation make sense?

targets.name: SOSV HAX
targets.role: GPs: Duncan Turner, Avra van der Zee
targets.why: HAX is SOSV's hard-tech pre-seed program (up to $550K) and lists health tech as a focus. It co-invested in Level Zero Health's $6.9M wearable hormone-monitor pre-seed, and HAX alum Samphire raised a $5M seed for a neurotech wearable.
targets.why_now: 2025-06-05: HAX alum Samphire $5M seed; 2025-02-18 Level Zero pre-seed with HAX participation
targets.ask: Application to HAX program
targets.opener: Hi HAX team - Vybe Health is a screenless ECG/HRV band from a veteran/woman/minority-owned team in Akron, sold as a licensed SDK/API. DevKit v0.1 goes to 5-10 design partners this fall, and we're scaling toward a May 2027 consumer launch. Manufacturing support is exactly what we need. Could we get 15 minutes before applying?

targets.name: Seaside Ventures
targets.why: Consumer health seed fund. Its portfolio lists Somnee (smart sleep headband, seed), and it joined Adaptyx's $14M biowearable seed. Its 'Medicine 3.0' thesis is proactive, personalized health.
targets.ask: 15-min intro call
targets.opener: Hi Harrison and Ryan - Seaside's bets on Somnee and Adaptyx are close to what we're building. Vybe Health is a screenless ECG/HRV band with a licensed SDK/API, no subscription, general wellness. DevKit v0.1 goes to 5-10 design partners this fall. Could we grab 15 minutes to see if it fits Fund I?

targets.name: Sunil Nagaraj
targets.why: Ubiquity participated in SOND's $7M round (in-ear HRV/SCG sleep sensing). Thesis is 'software beyond the screen': pre-seed/seed, $1M-$3M lead or co-lead checks into technical founders putting software into physical sensors and devices.
targets.ask: Send a concise deck note, ask for a 15-min call
targets.opener: Hi Sunil - Vybe Health is software beyond the screen in the most literal way: a screenless ECG/HRV band whose product is the SDK/API developers license. DevKit v0.1 ships to 5-10 design partners this fall; consumer launch May 2027. Saw Ubiquity in SOND. Happy to go deep on the board and firmware if you have 15 minutes.

targets.name: Ultrahuman raises $70M led by Qualcomm Ventures and opens ring to third-party developers
targets.why: On 4 Sep 2026 Ultrahuman announced $70M ($65M equity, $5M debt) led by Qualcomm Ventures at a $365M valuation, with Labcorp, Alpha Wave, Blume, Nexus and Alteria. It plans a software update so third-party developers can build apps for its rings. Qualcomm Ventures published its thesis on 24 Sep 2026 (Anirvan Chowdhury) on hardware+AI wearable platforms. A chip-maker CVC is now backing 'wearable as a developer platform', the same bet Vybe is making.
targets.ask: Message Anirvan Chowdhury (Qualcomm Ventures) referencing his Ultrahuman post; ask for a 15-minute conversation on band-based developer platforms.
targets.opener: Your Ultrahuman post argues wearables are becoming platforms that combine sensing, edge AI and developers. We are building that for the wrist: a screenless ECG/HRV band with a licensed SDK, and DevKit v0.1 is going to 5-10 design partners. Would you be open to a short conversation?

targets.name: a16z speedrun
targets.why: Backed Clair Health (cohort 006), a continuous-hormone wrist wearable, and joined its $11.6M seed. Speedrun invests up to $1M in very early companies.
targets.ask: Apply to next speedrun cohort
targets.opener: Hi speedrun team - applying with Vybe Health: a screenless ECG/HRV band sold as a developer platform (licensed SDK/API, DevKit v0.1 to 5-10 design partners). Clair showed you'll back hardware-plus-data early. Happy to walk through the board and SDK in 15 minutes.

targets.name: Google launches $99 screenless Fitbit Air; Fitbit app becomes Google Health
targets.why: Fitbit Air, announced in May 2026 and available 26 May, is a $99 screenless band with optical HR, SpO2 sensors and skin-temperature variation. It works on iOS and Android through the new Google Health app, and most features need no subscription. It launched in India in late September 2026. A $99 Google band sets a low consumer price anchor; Vybe should compete on raw ECG and developer access, not consumer price.
targets.ask: Make sure Vybe's positioning is 'ECG + open SDK for builders', not 'cheaper WHOOP'; add Fitbit Air to the competitor table.

targets.name: Apple prototyping screenless fitness band (Gurman); launch not before 2028
targets.why: On 23 Sep 2026 Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reported that Apple is prototyping a screenless fabric fitness band with a sensor module, as part of a rethink of the Apple Watch line. It is still at the investigation stage and not expected before 2028. This confirms the screenless form factor, and Vybe has about 18 months of lead time before Apple could enter.
targets.ask: Put 'Apple validates screenless; not shipping before 2028' on the investor 'why now' slide.

targets.name: Google Fit APIs (incl. REST) deprecated in 2026; no REST replacement
targets.why: Google's own migration FAQ says the Google Fit APIs, including the REST API, are deprecated in 2026, sign-ups closed 1 May 2024, and 'there is no alternative to the Fit REST API' beyond Health Connect (on-device) or the Google Health API. Second Google sunset in the same window widens the pool of builders who need a stable wearable data source.
targets.why_now: Deprecation during 2026 (supported until end of 2026 per migration docs)
targets.ask: Ship a Health Connect write path in the Vybe SDK roadmap and say so on the DevKit page; target Google Fit REST users in outreach.
targets.opener: Google Fit REST goes away this year and Health Connect is on-device only. We are building a band plus SDK that gives developers direct ECG/HRV access, and we plan to write into Health Connect too. Would a 15-minute call on your post-Fit data plan be useful?

targets.name: Level Zero Health $6.9M pre-seed for continuous hormone wearable
targets.why: On 18 Feb 2025 Level Zero Health (female-founded, London) closed a $6.9M oversubscribed pre-seed, which Tech.eu reported as a European record for a female-founded company. Backers include redalpine, HAX (SOSV), Entrepreneur First, Unruly Capital, Exceptional Ventures, Samos, Anorak, Springbank Collective, DTX and Black Jays. HAX/SOSV and Springbank are pre-seed hardware and women-focused funds Vybe qualifies for.
targets.ask: Approach HAX (SOSV) and Springbank Collective; both write pre-seed checks in hardware or women-led health.
targets.opener: You backed Level Zero's pre-seed wearable. Vybe Health is a woman-, veteran- and minority-owned team building a screenless ECG/HRV band and SDK for developers, with DevKit v0.1 shipping to design partners. Would you be open to a short conversation?

targets.name: Quinn Li
targets.why: Qualcomm Ventures backed Ultrahuman's $70M round. Ultrahuman is building a Qualcomm-silicon ring that developers can program. Li called personal AI devices 'ambient and always on'. Vybe's SDK-first band fits this platform thesis.
targets.ask: 15-min intro call
targets.opener: Hi Quinn - Ultrahuman's plan to let developers run code on the ring is exactly our thesis. Vybe Health is a screenless ECG/HRV band whose product is a licensed SDK/API; DevKit v0.1 goes to 5-10 design partners this fall. I'd value 15 minutes on how Qualcomm Ventures looks at early wearable platforms.

targets.name: Redalpine
targets.why: Led Level Zero Health's $6.9M pre-seed for a wearable hormone-monitoring patch, described as the largest pre-seed by a female-founded company in Europe. Redalpine invests at the intersection of software and science.
targets.ask: 15-min intro call
targets.opener: Hi Redalpine team - your Level Zero pre-seed caught my eye. Vybe Health is a woman/veteran/minority-owned US team building a screenless ECG/HRV band and licensed SDK/API for developers. DevKit v0.1 goes to design partners this fall. I know we're outside your core geography; would you still take a 15-minute conversation?

targets.name: WHOOP raises $575M Series G at $10.1B led by Collaborative Fund
targets.why: WHOOP's Series G closed in late March 2026 at a $10.1B valuation. Collaborative Fund (Craig Shapiro) led and called it the firm's largest investment ever. Other participants include QIA, Mubadala, Macquarie, Mayo Clinic, IVP, Foundry, and Abbott as a strategic. WHOOP reports 2.5M+ members and a $1.1B run rate. Collaborative backed WHOOP early from Fund II, which shows it will go from seed to late stage in wearables.
targets.ask: Send Collaborative Fund a short note pointing to Craig Shapiro's 'Health OS' post: Vybe is the open developer-platform layer underneath.
targets.opener: Craig's WHOOP letter frames the body as needing a software layer that keeps up. We are building the open version for developers: a screenless ECG/HRV band with a licensed SDK, no subscription, general wellness only. Would someone on the team take a 15-minute call?

targets.name: Wearlinq $14M Series A (AIX Ventures) for wireless 6-lead ECG wearable
targets.why: On 17 Dec 2025 Wearlinq raised a $14M Series A plus $5M venture debt for eWave, a wireless 6-lead ECG monitor. AIX Ventures led, with SpringTide, Berkeley Catalyst Fund, Lightscape, Solasta, Alumni Ventures, Amino Capital, Angelschool, LDV Partners, Maliam, XB Ventures, Celtic House Asia Partners Health, Device of Tomorrow Capital, NYX Ventures and SmartLink. This syndicate has recently backed ECG wearable hardware.
targets.ask: Target Device of Tomorrow Capital, Berkeley Catalyst Fund and Angelschool from the syndicate for seed conversations on wellness ECG.
targets.opener: You backed Wearlinq's wireless ECG, so you know the hardware. Vybe Health is building the general-wellness version as a developer platform: a screenless ECG/HRV band with a licensed SDK, and DevKit v0.1 is going to 5-10 design partners. Open to a 15-minute conversation?

targets.name: Oura API cuts off Gen3 users without paid membership
targets.why: Oura's partner support page (updated 26 Aug 2026) says Gen3 ring users without an active membership can no longer access data through the Oura API, and neither can partner apps. Data access on incumbent wearables is tied to subscriptions. This supports Vybe's no-subscription, developer-first access pitch to builders.
targets.ask: Put 'your users' data access never depends on a subscription' on the DevKit landing page.

targets.name: FDA closes WHOOP warning letter on Blood Pressure Insights
targets.why: FDA sent WHOOP a warning letter on 14 Jul 2025 over Blood Pressure Insights. In June 2026 it posted a close-out letter saying it will not enforce device rules on the modified feature, in line with the January wellness guidance. This is a working example of how wording, display ranges and claims decide whether a wellness feature counts as a device.
targets.ask: Use the WHOOP close-out as a reference when writing Vybe's display and claims rules for SDK partners.

targets.name: Amazfit Helio Strap ($99) and Helio Strap Pro for HYROX
targets.why: The Amazfit Helio Strap launched in June 2025 as a $99 subscription-free WHOOP alternative that can be worn on the wrist or arm. In June 2026 the Helio Strap Pro added a waist motion pod aimed at HYROX strength metrics. Budget bands are crowding the bottom of the market, and HYROX athletes are a real niche to target.
targets.ask: Consider HYROX coaches and apps as early DevKit design partners; Amazfit's move shows the segment is underserved.

targets.name: Google Health API adds ECG, IRN and HRV webhooks
targets.why: Release notes dated 26 May 2026 add .ecg.readonly and .irn.readonly scopes, an electrocardiogram data type, paired-device endpoints and webhooks for heart-rate variability and other types. On 17 Aug 2026 women's-health write scopes were added. The new Google aggregation layer will be where many developers look for wearable data, so Vybe data should show up there.
targets.ask: Investigate whether third-party devices can write ECG/HRV into Google Health / Health Connect, and plan Vybe as a source in that ecosystem.

targets.name: Lunar Ventures
targets.why: Led Emm's $9M seed for a sensor-embedded smart menstrual cup, a biowearable. Lunar backs technical founders from day zero in deep tech.
targets.ask: 15-min intro call
targets.opener: Hi Lunar team - congrats on Emm. Vybe Health is a technical hardware team building a screenless ECG/HRV band whose product is a licensed SDK/API for developers. DevKit v0.1 goes to 5-10 design partners this fall. Would you be open to a 15-minute call even though we're US-based?

targets.name: Point Nine
targets.why: Participated in Junction's $18M Series A. Junction (formerly Vital) is an API unifying data from 500+ health wearables and lab networks. Point Nine is a seed-first fund ($1-10M checks) investing in AI for the physical and biological world, a close fit for Vybe's SDK/API model.
targets.why_now: 2025-04-10: participated in Junction $18M Series A (wearable data API)
targets.ask: 15-min intro call
targets.opener: Hi Point Nine team - you backed Junction's bet that wearable data needs real infrastructure. Vybe Health builds the device side of that: a screenless ECG/HRV band sold as a licensed SDK/API, with DevKit v0.1 going to 5-10 design partners this fall. Would a partner be open to 15 minutes?

targets.name: Sahha raises $1.2M for wearable data API (Antler, Supermoon, Func Ventures)
targets.why: On 21 Jul 2025 Sahha (wearable/health data API across 300+ devices) raised $1.2M, bringing its total to $4M. Supermoon Capital, Aura Ventures and Antler followed on, with new money from Gandel Invest, Func Ventures and Cutri Family Office. Sahha also publishes the Fitbit-shutdown migration guide, so it could be both a distribution partner for Vybe data and a source of investor names.
targets.ask: Ask Sahha to add Vybe as a supported device source; separately ask Antler/Supermoon about dev-platform wearables.
targets.opener: Your Fitbit shutdown guide is the clearest we have read. We are building a screenless ECG/HRV band with a licensed SDK and would like Vybe to be a source in Sahha. Could we do a 15-minute call on what a clean integration looks like?

targets.name: True Ventures
targets.why: First-check seed fund. In 2025-2026 it backed Sandbar's $13M round for the Stream smart ring and led Channel Robotics' $2.5M Seed+ for a handheld endoscopic robotics device. It actively funds wearable and health hardware.
targets.why_now: 2025-11-05: Sandbar launches Stream smart ring with $13M from True Ventures, Upfront, Betaworks; 2026 Channel Robotics Seed+ led by True
targets.ask: 15-min intro call
targets.opener: Hi True team - between Sandbar and Channel Robotics you're writing first checks into body-worn and health hardware. Vybe Health is a screenless ECG/HRV band whose product is a licensed SDK/API; DevKit v0.1 goes to 5-10 design partners this fall. Would you be open to a 15-minute conversation?

targets.name: Vaark Ventures
targets.why: Led Theta Neurotech's $2M pre-seed for a behind-the-ear EEG wearable patch (Chicago). Co-investors were UChicago Medicine Ventures and Band of Angels.
targets.ask: 15-min intro call
targets.opener: Hi Vaark team - saw you led Theta's pre-seed. Vybe Health is a Midwest (Akron, OH) team building a screenless ECG/HRV band whose product is a licensed SDK/API, with DevKit v0.1 going to design partners this fall. Would you be open to a 15-minute call?

targets.name: HHS Secretary Kennedy: 'every American wearing a wearable within four years'
targets.why: At a House Energy & Commerce hearing on 24 Jun 2025, HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. said HHS is preparing 'one of the biggest advertising campaigns in HHS history' to promote wearables and wants every American wearing one within four years. Federal tailwind for consumer wellness wearables (and for a Vybe veteran/HHS-adjacent narrative), but privacy concerns are rising.
targets.ask: Reference the HHS goal in grant applications and the deck; lead Vybe's privacy messaging with user-owned data.

targets.name: ITC bans Ultrahuman rings in US over Oura patents; RingConn takes license
targets.why: ITC exclusion and cease-and-desist orders took effect on 21 Oct 2025 and blocked imports and sales of Ultrahuman rings in the US. RingConn settled with a multi-year royalty license. Ultrahuman lost about half its users' market until it redesigned. IP in wearable form factors is now actively enforced, so Vybe should run freedom-to-operate checks before its May 2027 launch.
targets.ask: Commission a freedom-to-operate review of band and sensor-module patents (WHOOP, Oura, Polar) before DevKit v0.1 ships.

targets.name: Polar Loop: $199.99 screenless band, no subscription
targets.why: On 3 Sep 2025 Polar launched the Loop ($199.99, shipping 10 Sep), a consumer version of its B2B Polar 360 with 8-day battery and no subscription fee. The Polar 360 B2B heritage shows a band can be sold both to businesses (research, teams) and to consumers, a similar dual path to Vybe's DevKit-then-consumer plan.
targets.ask: Study Polar 360's B2B licensing and partner model as a template for Vybe's DevKit pricing.

targets.name: WHOOP 5.0 / MG launch with $199-$359/yr membership tiers
targets.why: On 8 May 2025 WHOOP launched WHOOP 5.0 and WHOOP MG with on-demand ECG (Heart Screener), Blood Pressure Insights, 14-day battery and three annual tiers: One $199, Peak $239, Life $359. That made 'medical-grade' ECG on a screenless band a mainstream expectation, sold through a subscription.
targets.ask: Use WHOOP's $359/yr ECG tier as the price anchor when showing Vybe's one-time-purchase plus licensing model.

targets.name: AIX Ventures
targets.why: Led Wearlinq's $14M Series A for eWave, an FDA-cleared wireless 6-lead ECG wearable. AIX is an AI-focused fund, and ECG wearables plus ML is Vybe's core overlap.
targets.ask: 15-min intro call
targets.opener: Hi AIX team - congrats on Wearlinq. Vybe Health is building the wellness-side counterpart: a screenless ECG/HRV band whose product is a licensed SDK/API so developers can train and ship models on clean cardiac signals. DevKit v0.1 goes to design partners this fall. Open to 15 minutes?

targets.name: Blume Ventures
targets.why: Led Mave Health's $2.1M seed (neuromodulation headset, San Francisco/Bengaluru) and participated in Ultrahuman's $70M smart-ring round. Blume is a repeat wearable backer.
targets.why_now: 2026-09-03: in Ultrahuman $70M round; Mave seed lead announced 2026-03-18
targets.ask: Feedback call; possible co-investor
targets.opener: Hi Blume team - with Ultrahuman and Mave in your portfolio, you know wearables well. Vybe Health is a US team building a screenless ECG/HRV band whose product is a licensed SDK/API. I'd value 15 minutes of feedback on positioning a platform-first wearable at seed.

targets.name: Humba Ventures
targets.why: Hard-tech pre-seed/seed fund that participated in Adaptyx's $14M seed for a continuous molecular-monitoring wearable.
targets.ask: 15-min intro call
targets.opener: Hi Humba team - saw you in Adaptyx's seed. Vybe Health is a hard-tech wearable company: screenless ECG/HRV band, our own firmware, sold as a licensed SDK/API to developers. DevKit v0.1 goes to design partners this fall. Would you be up for a 15-minute call on the hardware plan?

targets.name: JumpStart Ventures
targets.why: Ohio's early-stage fund ($140M across funds) investing from seed to Series A. Healthcare is a focus area. It runs a Focus Fund for underrepresented Ohio founders and a Healthcare Collaboration Fund with University Hospitals Ventures. This is the founder-identity and Ohio network path.
targets.warm_path: Ohio (Akron, Northeast Ohio); minority/woman-founder Focus Fund
targets.ask: Intro meeting with JumpStart healthcare investment team
targets.opener: Hi JumpStart team - Vybe Health is an Akron-based, veteran/woman/minority-owned company building a screenless ECG/HRV band with a licensed SDK/API for developers. DevKit v0.1 goes to 5-10 design partners this fall, consumer launch May 2027. We'd love 15 minutes to see if the Focus or Healthcare Collaboration Fund fits.

targets.name: Rock Health H1 2026: $7.4B digital health funding; wearables are the platform story
targets.why: On 13 Jul 2026 Rock Health reported that US digital health startups raised $7.4B across 244 deals in H1 2026, up from $6.4B, with mega-deals taking 45% of capital. Oura's S-1 and WHOOP's $575M round were cited as signs that wearables are becoming consumer health platforms. Forbes (31 Jul 2026) called wearables a standout. Useful as a funding-climate slide.
targets.ask: Cite in the seed deck 'why now' slide; note capital is concentrated, so the seed pitch should stay narrow.

targets.name: Eli Lilly makes equity investment in Oura after LillyDirect GLP-1 tie-up
targets.why: Oura and LillyDirect announced a GLP-1 support collaboration on 23 Jun 2026, and Lilly made an undisclosed equity investment in Oura on 15 Jul 2026. Pharma is now buying into wearables for adherence and metabolic support. Pharma and metabolic programs could become licensing customers for Vybe's SDK.
targets.ask: Add 'pharma adherence programs' as a later-stage licensing segment; no outreach to Lilly yet.

targets.name: IDC: 611.5M wearables shipped in 2025; 625.2M forecast for 2026; wrist-worn down 4.3% in Q2 2026
targets.why: LEAP:IN (16 Jun 2026), citing IDC, reports 2025 wearable shipments up 9.1% to 611.5M, a 2026 forecast of 625.2M (+2.2%) and about 690M by 2030; wristbands grew 14.7% in 2025. TechNode reported on 9 Sep 2026 that IDC counted Q2 2026 wrist-worn shipments at 48.01M (-4.3%), with fitness bands at 10.92M (-4.7%). Unit growth is slowing, so differentiation (ECG, SDK) matters more than volume.
targets.ask: Use IDC figures (cited via secondary sources) on the market slide; buy or confirm IDC primary data before external use.

targets.name: Interlagos
targets.why: Led Adaptyx Biosciences' $14M seed for a continuous multi-analyte molecular-monitoring wearable.
targets.ask: Intro via Adaptyx co-investor (Overwater/Seaside)
targets.opener: Hi - congrats on leading Adaptyx's seed. We're building Vybe Health, a screenless ECG/HRV band with a licensed SDK/API for developers; DevKit v0.1 goes to 5-10 design partners this fall. If wearable data platforms are a theme for you, I'd value a 15-minute conversation.

targets.name: Inventure
targets.why: Led Samphire Neuroscience's $5M seed for a wearable neurotech headband. Inventure is a Nordic/Baltic seed fund and features the Samphire deal on its homepage.
targets.ask: Feedback call on wearable seed positioning
targets.opener: Hi Inventure team - your Samphire thesis on overlooked health categories resonated. Vybe Health is a US team building a screenless ECG/HRV band with a developer SDK/API. I know we're outside your Nordic focus, so I'd mainly value 15 minutes of feedback on how you evaluated a wearable at seed.

targets.name: Oura raises $900M+ Series E at $11B (Fidelity lead)
targets.why: On 14 Oct 2025 Oura announced a Series E of over $900M at an $11B valuation. Fidelity led, with new investor ICONIQ plus Whale Rock and Atreides. Oura reported more than $500M of 2024 revenue and 5.5M rings sold. These are late-stage crossover funds, not seed investors, but the round sets the category comp Vybe's investors will cite.
targets.ask: Use as a category comp in the seed deck; do not cold-pitch the late-stage leads.

targets.name: Rev1 Ventures
targets.why: Columbus venture studio and investor backing SaaS/AI, deep tech and life sciences startups across the Midwest. Rev1-supported founders were behind more than half of Central Ohio's 55 deals in 2025, which makes it the Ohio network path.
targets.ask: Intro meeting with Rev1 deep tech / life sciences team
targets.opener: Hi Rev1 team - Vybe Health is an Ohio company (Akron) building a screenless ECG/HRV band and licensed SDK/API, from a veteran/woman/minority-owned team. DevKit v0.1 goes to design partners this fall. Could we set up 15 minutes to see whether Rev1's studio or capital is a fit?

targets.name: Samsung completes Xealth acquisition to wire wearable data into clinical workflows
targets.why: Samsung closed its acquisition of Xealth on 17 Oct 2025 (announced in July). Xealth works with 30+ health systems and 500 hospitals, and Samsung aims to bring Galaxy wearable data into clinician workflows and EHRs. Big platforms are buying the clinical-integration layer, which raises the value of wellness wearable data that can be integrated.
targets.ask: Note in the deck that wearable-to-clinic integration is drawing strategic M&A; keep Vybe wellness-only but integration-ready.

targets.name: Xsensio €6M Series A (WI Harper) for wearable biochemical sensing chip
targets.why: On 3 Mar 2026 Xsensio (Lausanne) closed an oversubscribed €6M Series A led by WI Harper with Privilège Ventures and the European Innovation Council. EU-Startups lists a wider 2025-26 European wearable biosensing funding run (Sava €16.6M, Level Zero, Liom €13.9M). WI Harper is a cross-border deep-tech investor active in wearable sensing.
targets.ask: Add WI Harper to the investor long-list for a later round; low priority now.

targets.name: YC W26 'Fort' building a screenless strength-tracking band
targets.why: Fort, a Y Combinator Winter 2026 company founded by ex-Tesla engineers, launched on 2 Feb 2026 with a screenless band that auto-detects strength exercises, reps and fatigue from motion and heart rate. The YC Spring 2026 batch also includes Anoria, an emotion-sensing bracelet. YC is funding wearable hardware again, so there are new hardware builders who may prefer licensing a sensor platform over building one.
targets.ask: Ask Fort (and similar YC wearable teams) whether a licensed ECG/HRV module plus SDK would shorten their roadmap; possible design partner or co-marketing.
targets.opener: Fort's strength-tracking band looks great. We are building a screenless ECG/HRV band with a licensed SDK and wonder whether our sensor data could complement your motion models. Open to a 15-minute call?

targets.name: Hume Band 2.0: $249 one-time, no subscription, BP trend insights
targets.why: Hume Health sells the screenless Hume Band 2.0 for $249 one-time with no subscription and a 14-day battery, marketing BP trend insights, HRV and Pace of Aging. Its page compares a 2-year cost of $249 vs WHOOP $697+ and Oura $438+. A direct no-subscription consumer comp for Vybe's May 2027 launch. (Not to be confused with Hume AI.)
targets.ask: Add Hume to the pricing comp; note it competes on consumer price, while Vybe offers ECG plus developer access.
